title: Upstream log: problems the brms-parity loop found in brms, Stan Math and loo
about: Each entry is a place where brms, the Stan Math library as shipped with rstan's StanHeaders, or loo computes something wrong or inexactly, or accepts input it should refuse, found while AutoBayes was compared with brms (`docs/brms-parity/divergences.md`). Nothing here has been posted anywhere.

Every entry has a standalone R script that needs only CRAN brms, rstan and loo (no AutoBayes): it prints what the library gives next to the exact value, which it computes itself from a closed form or a stable log-space formula, and exits with status 1 while the problem is present. Densities and gradients come from `brm(..., chains = 0)` with `rstan::log_prob` and `grad_log_prob` (the prior's part removed by evaluating the same compiled model with its `prior_only` flag set); predictions from fixed-parameter runs. Nothing samples.

The fixes are described from the mathematics. brms's, loo's and Stan's source code was not read; where a cause is inferred from outputs it is said so. Known-upstream status comes from read-only searches of brms's NEWS and the paul-buerkner/brms, stan-dev/math and stan-dev/loo issue trackers.

entries.title: hurdle_negbinomial `posterior_predict()` does not draw the positive part from the zero-truncated negative binomial

found.note: Recorded in `tests/zero_hurdle_probes`; reproduced independently in the Tier D review.

entries.what: The share of zeros is right (`hu`), but the positive draws are too concentrated at 1 and their mean is too small, so the draws contradict brms's own `posterior_epred()`, which reports the zero-truncated mean.
entries.observed: At `mu = 0.5, shape = 0.5, hu = 0.05` (fixed-parameter run, 100000 draws, 95122 positive): P(y = 1 | y > 0) = 0.8164 and E[y | y > 0] = 1.2709. At `mu = 3, shape = 2`: 0.2608 and 3.1557. At `mu = 0.05, shape = 0.2`: 0.9774 and 1.0246. `posterior_epred()` gives 1.621751442, 3.392857143 and 1.088263927, the exact values.
entries.expected: The zero-truncated negative binomial: P(y = 1 | y > 0) = 0.6036, 0.2286, 0.8764 and E[y | y > 0] = `mu / (1 - NB(0))` = 1.7071, 3.5714, 1.1455 (between 24 and 134 standard errors from brms's draws).
entries.fix: Draw the positive part by inverting the survival function on its own range: `v ~ Uniform(0, 1 - NB(0))`, `y = qnbinom(v, size = shape, mu = mu, lower.tail = FALSE)`, which is exactly the zero-truncated distribution and has no rejection loop when NB(0) is near 1.

entries.title: `posterior_epred()` of a count response with `trunc(lb = )` starts the support at lb + 1 and cuts it off near 3 mu
functions: trunc() for negbinomial (and the other count families)
entries.what: The likelihood of `y | trunc(lb = 1)` is normalised by P(Y >= 1), but the expected value is the mean over 2..M with a finite M, so it is neither E[Y | Y >= 1] nor E[Y | Y >= 2].
entries.observed: Negative binomial `y | trunc(lb = 1) ~ 1`: at `mu = 1.5, shape = 1` brms gives 2.673469388 = the mean over 2..4; at `mu = 134, shape = 0.6` it gives 102.6108362 = the mean over 2..402, whatever the data's largest count (5 or 300). On the frozen case `negbinomial_truncated` (point 7, row 27) 106.236, the mean over 2..394.
entries.expected: E[Y | Y >= 1] = `mu / (1 - NB(0))`: 2.5 and 139.4172675 (106.236 should be 133.95). The likelihood (checked with `log_prob`) is normalised by P(Y >= 1), so the expected value must be that distribution's.
entries.fix: For a lower bound alone use the closed form `E[Y | Y >= lb] = (mu - sum_{k < lb} k P(k)) / (1 - F(lb - 1))`, which needs no truncation of the support; with both bounds sum `k P(k)` over `lb..ub` and divide by `F(ub) - F(lb - 1)`.

known_upstream.summary: Known: the lb + 1 start is brms issue #1923, fixed by PR #1926 in the development version

entries.title: cumulative("cloglog") forms its upper categories' probabilities by subtraction; the log density loses them and is -Inf beyond d of about 3.6

found.note: The link was accepted on a narrower case (#79); the frozen case `cumulative_cloglog` keeps its G2 gates expected to fail.

entries.what: The last category's probability is `1 - inv_cloglog(d)` and the others `inv_cloglog(d_k) - inv_cloglog(d_{k-1})`, formed by subtraction of numbers near 1, so an improbable category keeps only a few digits, and none once `inv_cloglog(d)` rounds to 1.
entries.observed: Intercept-only model, one row per category, thresholds (-1, 3, 3.375) (P = 0.308, 0.692, 1.89e-9, 2.03e-13): log likelihood -50.85601389939049, gradient off by up to 1.0e-4 relative. Thresholds (-1, 3, 4) (P(y = 4) = 1.94e-24): log likelihood -Inf, gradient -Inf. On the frozen case `cumulative_cloglog` the log density is 5.9e-7 relative off (1.45e-4 absolute) and the gradient up to 1.3e-4.
entries.expected: -50.85611467237852 (relative error 2e-6) and -76.22987349665763, with finite gradients; at the control thresholds (-1, 0, 1) brms agrees to 1.4e-16.
entries.fix: Evaluate every category on the log scale from the survival function `S(d) = 1 - inv_cloglog(d) = exp(-exp(d))`, with `d_k = tau_k - eta`: `log P(y = 1) = log1m_exp(-exp(d_1))`, `log P(y = K) = -exp(d_{K-1})`, and `log P(y = k) = -exp(d_{k-1}) + log1m_exp(-(exp(d_k) - exp(d_{k-1})))` (that is, `log_diff_exp` of the two log survival values).

entries.title: The Beta family forms `1 - mu` by subtraction: digits lost, and `beta_lpdf` rejects the draw once mu rounds to 1
entries.what: The second shape is `(1 - mu) * phi` with `1 - mu` by subtraction: it loses `eps / (1 - mu)` relative, and is exactly 0 above eta of about 37 (logit), 8.25 (probit; Stan's Phi is 1 there) and 3.6 (cloglog), where Stan's `beta_lpdf` raises an error and the draw is rejected.
entries.observed: y = 0.5, phi = 5: logit eta = 30 gives -30.47102418467954 (relative error 3.3e-5), eta = 40 an error (`beta_lpdf: Second shape parameter[1] is 0`); probit eta = 8 gives -35.41504472969478 (1.9e-3), eta = 9 the error; cloglog eta = 3.4 gives -30.4337238232663 (1.2e-5), eta = 3.7 the error.
entries.fix: Take `1 - mu` from the link's other tail instead of subtracting: `inv_logit(-eta)`, `Phi(-eta)`, `exp(-exp(eta))`, and pass `beta_lpdf(y | mu * phi, q * phi)` with that `q`. (Where even `q` underflows, about eta = 37.5 for probit, the shape needs `lgamma` from `log q`.)

entries.title: Bernoulli and binomial cloglog likelihoods form a failure's `log(1 - theta)` from `theta = inv_cloglog(eta)`

found.note: Accepted with a 50-digit reference for the gradient (P6, #47).

entries.what: `bernoulli_lpmf(y | inv_cloglog(eta))` (and the binomial's) differentiates and evaluates `log(1 - theta)` after `theta` has rounded: the gradient loses about `eps * exp(exp(eta))` relative, and the log density of a failure is -Inf once theta rounds to 1 (eta of about 3.6), where the exact value is `-exp(eta)`.
entries.observed: Bernoulli y = 0: eta = 3 log likelihood -20.08553689560981 (1.4e-9), gradient -20.08553636927165 (2.8e-8); eta = 3.5: -33.12588265703288 (3.1e-4), gradient -33.46267700016426 (1%); eta = 4: -Inf, gradient +Inf. Binomial 1 of 3: eta = 3.5 -65.15315302539764 (3.2e-4), eta = 4 -Inf. On the frozen case `bernoulli_cloglog` one gradient entry is 3.8e-7 off.
entries.fix: Write the likelihood on the log scale: a success adds `log1m_exp(-exp(eta))`, a failure `-exp(eta)`; the binomial `y log1m_exp(-exp(eta)) - (n - y) exp(eta)` plus the log binomial coefficient.

entries.title: Bernoulli and binomial probit likelihoods are -Inf where Stan's Phi saturates (eta above 8.25 for a failure, below -37.5 for a success)
entries.what: `bernoulli_lpmf(y | Phi(eta))`: Stan's `Phi` is exactly 1 above 8.25 and 0 below -37.5, so `log(1 - theta)` of a failure is -Inf above 8.25 (and loses digits from about 5), and `log(theta)` of a success is -Inf below -37.5, with infinite or NaN gradients.
entries.observed: Bernoulli y = 0: eta = 5 -15.06499839422134 (1.5e-11), eta = 8 -34.94504110044905 (2e-3; gradient 6.6% off), eta = 8.5 and 9 -Inf. Bernoulli y = 1: eta = -38 -Inf (gradient +Inf), eta = -40 -Inf (gradient NaN). Binomial 0 of 3: eta = 8 -104.8351233013471, eta = 9 -Inf.
entries.fix: Use the log CDF: a success adds `std_normal_lcdf(eta)`, a failure `std_normal_lcdf(-eta)` (binomial: `y std_normal_lcdf(eta) + (n - y) std_normal_lcdf(-eta)` plus the log coefficient). Its value is exact in double precision down to -40 in these probes; its derivative carries U23's error until Stan Math fixes that.

entries.title: Hurdle and zero-inflated Poisson densities and the hurdle mean break at extreme linear predictors (+Inf, infinite or NaN gradients, NaN mean)
entries.what: A hurdle y > 0 row subtracts `log1m_exp(-exp(eta))`, which is `log(0)` once `exp(eta)` underflows, so the row's log density is +Inf; a zero-inflated zero's gradient is NaN once `exp(eta)` overflows; the hurdle mean `mu / (1 - exp(-mu)) * (1 - hu)` is 0/0 where mu underflows.
entries.observed: hurdle_poisson, y = 1, hu = 0.3: eta = -740 log likelihood -0.3592542790478319 with gradient -Inf; eta = -750 +Inf with gradient NaN. zero_inflated_poisson, y = 0, zi = 0.3, eta = 710: value -1.203972804325936 (right) with gradient NaN. `posterior_epred()` at eta = -750: NaN.
entries.expected: y = 1: `log(1 - hu) - mu/2` = -0.3566749439387422 at both points with gradient about 0; the zero-inflated zero `log(zi)` with gradient (0, 1 - zi); the hurdle mean's limit `1 - hu` = 0.7. At eta = 0 brms agrees to 2e-16.
entries.fix: Evaluate `log(1 - exp(-mu))`, `mu = exp(eta)`, as `eta + log1p(-mu / 2)` below eta of about -20 (and `log(-expm1(-mu))` above), so it never forms `log(0)`; the zero-inflated zero as `log_sum_exp(log(zi), log1m(zi) - exp(eta))`, whose gradient is 0 where the second term is -Inf; the hurdle mean as `(1 - hu) exp(eta - log(1 - exp(-mu)))` with the same stable form (its limit 1 - hu).

entries.title: `log_lik()` is -Inf, +Inf or NaN (or inexact) at extreme but finite linear predictors
functions: waic() (R-side log-likelihoods of bernoulli, binomial, hurdle_poisson, cumulative, mixture)

found.note: The mixture case was described from brms's source in the row; here it is shown from output.

entries.what: The pointwise log-likelihood is evaluated in R from probabilities that round to 0 or 1, and a mixture's from a sum of component densities without factoring the largest out.
entries.observed: Bernoulli logit y = 0: eta = 35.07 gives -34.94504110044905 (3.6e-3), eta = 40 -Inf. Binomial 0 of 3: eta = 27.2 -81.60011489079963 (1.4e-6), eta = 40 -Inf. hurdle_poisson y = 1: eta = -26.9 -0.3566877935318438 (3.6e-5), eta = -60 +Inf. cumulative logit (-1, 0, 1): y = 4 at eta = -640 -Inf, y = 2 at eta = -640 NaN (with brms's warning that NAs were found). Two-Gaussian mixture at y = 40: -Inf.
entries.fix: Evaluate each row on the log scale, as the Stan model does: logit `y eta - log1p_exp(eta)` (binomial `y eta - n log1p_exp(eta)` plus the coefficient); the hurdle as in U07; ordinal categories from `log_inv_logit_diff` or `plogis(., log.p = TRUE)` of the tail; a mixture as `log_sum_exp` over `log theta_k + log p_k`.

entries.title: Cumulative `posterior_epred()` forms category probabilities by subtraction, losing digits between close thresholds
entries.what: P(y = k) is `plogis(tau_k - eta) - plogis(tau_{k-1} - eta)`, so a category between two close thresholds, or one small next to its neighbours in the upper tail, keeps only some of its digits.
entries.fix: `plogis(b) - plogis(a) = plogis(a) * plogis(-b) * expm1(b - a)` for `b > a` (no difference formed), or the exponential of the `log_inv_logit_diff` form the Stan code uses; the last category as `plogis(eta - tau_{K-1})`.

entries.title: Truncated Gaussian `posterior_epred()` loses its digits in the upper tail and is Inf or NaN beyond about 8.3 SD
functions: posterior_epred() of gaussian() with trunc() (R side)

found.note: Accepted with a 50-digit reference for these expected values (P6, #47).

entries.what: The truncated mean is formed with `pnorm(ub) - pnorm(lb)` by subtraction, so a bound several SD above the location loses the denominator's digits.
entries.fix: Compute the ratio on the log scale: for a lower bound alone `mu + sigma exp(dnorm(a, log = TRUE) - pnorm(a, lower.tail = FALSE, log.p = TRUE))`, `a = (lb - mu) / sigma`; with two bounds take `Phi(b) - Phi(a)` from the tail both lie in (`pnorm(a, lower.tail = FALSE) - pnorm(b, lower.tail = FALSE)` when `a > 0`) or in log space.

entries.title: Interval censoring takes the mass as `log_diff_exp` of two log CDFs, which loses every digit in the upper tail
functions: cens(c, y2) interval rows (generated Stan code)

found.note: E04's probes used rstan::expose_stan_functions; here the same numbers come from brms models. `weibull_censored_interval_post` could not be frozen on brms's default point box for this reason.

entries.what: An interval row (y, y2] gets `log_diff_exp(lcdf(y2), lcdf(y))`; in the upper tail both log CDFs are within a few eps of 0 (Stan 2.32's `weibull_lcdf(5 | 3, 1)` is 0 where the value is -exp(-125)), so the difference has no digits left. brms's own right-censored rows use the `lccdf` and are exact there.
entries.expected: -125 (the mass is exp(-125) - exp(-216)), -36.00000000000069 and -36.28648440797372, from the survival functions; the right-censored Weibull row at 5 (brms -125.0000000000001) and the controls (0.5, 1] and (1, 2] agree to 6e-16.
entries.fix: Choose the tail per row: when `F(y) > 1/2` use `log_diff_exp(lccdf(y), lccdf(y2))`, otherwise `log_diff_exp(lcdf(y2), lcdf(y))`. (Stan Math could also return the upper tail of its lcdfs accurately, e.g. `weibull_lcdf(y) = log1m_exp(-(y / sigma)^alpha)`, `gamma_lcdf = log1m(gamma_q)` above the median, but the tail choice in brms suffices for any version.)

entries.title: gen_extreme_value `posterior_epred()` is finite for xi > 1, NaN at xi = 0 and inexact near 0

found.note: brms 2.23 warns that the family is deprecated.

entries.what: The mean is evaluated as `mu + sigma (gamma(1 - xi) - 1) / xi` for every xi: for 1 < xi < 2 `gamma(1 - xi)` is negative and the 'mean' a finite negative number, though the mean is infinite for xi >= 1; at xi = 0 it is 0/0; near 0 `1 - xi` rounds away xi's low digits.
entries.observed: mu = 0.1, sigma = 1, xi fixed in the formula: xi = 1.5 gives -2.929938467874022, xi = 0 NaN, xi = 1e-10 0.6772160527328651 (5.7e-7 relative). With xi estimated (D114's probe) -1.9e-3 at xi = 9.82.
entries.expected: +Inf (no finite mean) for xi >= 1; `mu + sigma * euler` = 0.6772156649015323 at xi = 0; 0.6772156650004378 at xi = 1e-10; at the control xi = -0.5 brms is exact (0.3275461490944839).
entries.fix: Return +Inf (or NA with a warning) for xi >= 1; otherwise `mu + sigma * expm1(lgamma(1 - xi)) / xi` with `lgamma(1 - xi)` from its series `euler xi + sum_{k >= 2} zeta(k) xi^k / k` when |xi| is small, whose limit at xi = 0 is `mu + sigma * euler`.

entries.title: `gr(g, by = )`: the SD prior's truncation constant is added once per coefficient, not once per by level
functions: (1 | gr(g, by = gby)) (generated Stan code: lprior)

found.note: AutoBayes reproduces brms's constant (`1|g_sigma_by_normalisation`) to match it.

entries.what: Each of the Nby SD parameters has a half-normal (half-t, half-Cauchy) prior truncated at 0, but `lprior` adds `-log P(sd > 0) = log 2` only once per coefficient, so it is `(Nby - 1) log 2` too small. Sampling is unaffected; bridge sampling's marginal likelihood (and so Bayes factors) is off by that factor.
entries.observed: gby with 3 levels, sd ~ normal(0, 1): lprior -5.96256441474146.
entries.expected: -4.57627005362157, the difference -1.38629436111989 = -2 log 2; with gby of one level (the same compiled model) brms is exact (difference 4e-16).
entries.fix: Multiply the truncation term by the number of SD elements, `M x Nby`, so each SD parameter's prior is normalised on (0, Inf).

entries.title: Grouping factor `g:h` joins labels with "_", silently merging combinations whose joined labels coincide
entries.what: (g = "a_b", h = "c") and (g = "a", h = "b_c") both become "a_b_c" and so one group level, without a warning.
entries.observed: Three distinct (g, h) combinations: `N_1 = 2` levels, `J_1 = 1 1 2 1 1 2` (rows of (a_b, c) and (a, b_c) in level 1).
entries.expected: `N_1 = 3`, the two combinations in different levels.
entries.fix: Code the combined factor from the pair of levels (e.g. the pair's unique index, or `interaction(g, h, drop = TRUE)` with a separator that cannot occur in labels), or refuse joined labels that collide.

entries.title: A non-linear formula's integer division is Stan's in the model and R's in the predictions: `(1 / 2) * a` fits mu = 0 and predicts a / 2
entries.what: The expression is written into the Stan program as it stands, where `1 / 2` of two integer literals is integer division (0), and evaluated in R for predictions, where it is 0.5.
entries.observed: `bf(y ~ (1 / 2) * a, a ~ 1, nl = TRUE)`, y = 1, a = 2, sigma = 1: the model's log likelihood is -1.418938533204673 (that of mu = 0); `posterior_epred()` gives 1 (mu = 0.5 a).
entries.expected: One meaning in both: as R reads the formula, mu = 1 and the log likelihood -0.9189385332046728.
entries.fix: Write numeric literals into the Stan program as reals (`1` as `1.0`), so that Stan divides as R does, or refuse an integer division in a non-linear formula.

entries.title: Functions Stan does not have (`plogis()`, and `gp()`, `mo()`, `ar()` written in the expression) pass into a non-linear model's program unchecked
entries.what: brms writes the expression into the program without checking its functions, so the user gets a Stan semantic error instead of a message from brms (and `plogis()`, which brms's R-side predictions evaluate, is not translated to `inv_logit`).
entries.observed: `y ~ plogis(a * x)`, `y ~ a * gp(x)`, `y ~ a * mo(z)`, `y ~ a + ar(t)`: brms generates a program; Stan's compiler: "A returning function was expected but an undeclared identifier 'plogis' was supplied" (and 'gp', 'mo', 'ar').
entries.expected: A refusal from brms naming the function and what to write instead (or a translation of `plogis` to `inv_logit`); the control `y ~ inv_logit(a * x)` compiles.
entries.fix: Check each function name of a non-linear formula against the functions Stan and brms's Stan code provide before generating code, translating R's `plogis`, `qlogis`, `pnorm` to `inv_logit`, `logit`, `Phi` or refusing with a message, and refuse `gp()`, `mo()`, `ar()` inside the expression with a pointer to the parameter formulas.

entries.title: Under identity and inverse links a non-positive mean is returned by `posterior_epred()` without a word, and `posterior_predict()` draws NaN
entries.what: Stan rejects a draw whose mean leaves the family's support, but on new rows brms returns that mean as an expected value and draws NaN responses with only R's random-number warning. `Gamma("inverse")` is the Gamma family's default link.
entries.observed: b_Intercept = 1, b_x = 1, new row x = -2.33 (eta = -1.33): negbinomial identity and Gamma identity `posterior_epred` -1.33, Gamma inverse -0.75188, each with no error or warning; inverse.gaussian 1/mu^2 NaN (R's "NaNs produced"); `posterior_predict` NaN or NA with R's "NAs produced" / "NaNs produced".
entries.expected: An error, or NA with a warning naming the rows whose mean is outside the family's support (mu > 0; eta > 0 under 1/mu^2).
entries.fix: Check the predicted mean against the family's support in `posterior_epred()` and `posterior_predict()` (mu > 0 for the negative binomial, Gamma and inverse Gaussian; eta > 0 for the 1/mu^2 link) and stop, or return NA with a warning that names the rows, as for any other invalid input.

entries.title: asym_laplace accepts a fixed quantile of 0 or 1, where the density is 0 everywhere
entries.what: brms refuses a fixed quantile outside [0, 1] but accepts the end points, where the asymmetric Laplace density `q (1 - q) / sigma * exp(...)` is 0 for every response, so the model has log density -Inf everywhere.
entries.observed: `make_standata(bf(y ~ 1, quantile = 0))` and `quantile = 1`: accepted (1.5: refused, "Parameter 'quantile' must be between 0 and 1."); `dasym_laplace(., quantile = 0)` = 0, 0, 0; `log_prob` of the compiled model: -Inf.
entries.expected: Refuse quantile = 0 and 1 as well: the parameter must lie strictly between 0 and 1.
entries.fix: Require `0 < quantile < 1` for a fixed quantile (the open interval), with the same message.

entries.title: The default length-scale prior of `gp()` is solved to a tolerance coarser than the 6 decimals it is printed and written with

found.note: Rounding only: the prior differs from the correctly rounded one in the 6th decimal.

entries.what: The default `inv_gamma(a, b)` puts 1% of the mass below the smallest scaled distance between distinct inputs and 1% above the largest; brms's solver stops within about 1e-7 of the solution, which crosses a rounding boundary at some inputs.
entries.fix: Solve the one equation in the shape to double precision before rounding: with `1 / l ~ Gamma(a, rate b)`, `b = hi * qgamma(0.01, a)` and `pgamma(hi * qgamma(0.01, a) / lo, a) = 0.99` (bracketed root finding to about 1e-14), or write the unrounded values into the model.

entries.title: Approximate GP `gp(x, k = )`: NaN gradient wherever the spectral density underflows (every lscale above about 1 with k = 30)
functions: gp(x, k = , c = ) (generated Stan code: sqrt of the spectral density)

found.note: The divergence row records this as not probed; reproduced here.

entries.what: Basis function j is weighted by `sqrt(S(w_j))`, `S(w) = sdgp^2 sqrt(2 pi) lscale exp(-lscale^2 w^2 / 2)`. Where S underflows to 0 (`lscale * w_j` above about 38.6) the log density is finite but the chain rule through `sqrt` at 0 gives Inf times 0 = NaN in the gradient of sdgp and lscale. With k = 30 and c = 5/4 that is every lscale above 1.024 on brms's scaled inputs, an ordinary length-scale for a smooth function, where HMC cannot move.
entries.observed: `y ~ gp(x, k = 30, c = 5/4)`, 12 rows: at lscale = 1.2 and 2 the log density is finite (-58.82, -62.71) and the gradient in (log sdgp, log lscale) is (NaN, NaN), 2 of the 34 entries; at lscale = 0.5 all entries agree with a finite difference to 7e-9.
entries.expected: The finite gradient (4.3837865, -4.6773439) at lscale = 1.2 and (1.9224068, -9.2924243) at 2 (central finite differences of brms's own `log_prob`; the other 32 entries agree to 7e-9).
entries.fix: Form the weight without a square root of an underflowed number: `sqrt(S(w)) = sdgp (2 pi)^(1/4) sqrt(lscale) exp(-lscale^2 w^2 / 4)` (or `exp(0.5 * log S)` with `log S` computed directly), whose gradient is finite (and 0 in the limit) where S underflows.

entries.title: Stan's `normal_lccdf` loses its value in the upper tail (-Inf from z of about 8.3), so brms's right-censored rows are -Inf and truncated rows +Inf
functions: brms: gaussian() with cens() (right-censored rows) and trunc(lb = )

found.note: The value loss beyond z of about 5 and the -Inf from 8.3 were measured for this log; the divergence rows record the gradient (U23).

entries.what: `normal_lccdf(z | 0, 1)` = log(1 - Phi(z)) is off by 2.6e-12 relative at z = 5, 2.1e-9 at 6.17, 5.3e-4 at 8 and -Inf from about 8.3, where the value is an ordinary number. brms calls it for a right-censored Gaussian row and for a truncation's lower bound, so such a row 8.3 SD above its mean has log density -Inf, and a row of `y | trunc(lb = L)` with L 9 SD above the mean has log density +Inf (its density minus -Inf).
entries.fix: Evaluate the upper tail through the lower one, `normal_lccdf(y | mu, sigma) = std_normal_lcdf(-(y - mu) / sigma)` (Stan's `std_normal_lcdf` is exact in value to -40 in these probes), or from `log(erfc(z / sqrt 2) / 2)` with `erfc` (or `erfcx`) rather than `1 - erf`. brms can do the first today for any Stan version.

entries.title: Stan's `normal_lcdf` / `std_normal_lcdf` derivative is inexact (up to 2.3e-5 relative), and so are brms's censored Gaussian gradients
functions: brms: gaussian() with cens() and trunc()

found.note: `gauss_censored` and `gauss_truncated` are accepted against 50-digit references for their gradients (P6, #47).

entries.what: The value of log Phi(z) is accurate, but its derivative is not the inverse Mills ratio phi(z) / Phi(z) to double precision: it is off by 7e-7 at z = 1, 6.4e-6 at 2, 2.3e-5 at -10 and 1.3e-5 at -38, as if from a separate approximation; `normal_lccdf`'s derivative is off by 4.5e-8 at z = 6.17 and 1.9% at 8. brms's left- and right-censored (and truncated) Gaussian rows differentiate through them.
entries.expected: (-10.09809323396249, 100.9809323396249), (-0.05524786267898995, -0.1104957253579799) and (8.121368112236123, 64.97094489788898), from `m(z) = exp(dnorm(z, log = TRUE) - pnorm(z, log.p = TRUE))`; the right-censored row at z = 0 agrees to 1.4e-16. On the frozen cases: up to 2.5e-6 (`gauss_censored`) and 4.2e-7 (`gauss_truncated`) relative.
entries.fix: Differentiate the accurate value instead of an approximation: `d/dz log Phi(z) = phi(z) / Phi(z) = sqrt(2 / pi) / erfcx(-z / sqrt 2)` (with `erfcx`, now a Stan Math function), or `exp(log phi(z) - log Phi(z))` from the same log CDF the value uses.

entries.title: Stan's `gamma_lccdf` derivative in the shape is inexact (up to 1.2e-2 relative), and so are brms's right-censored Gamma gradients

found.note: `gamma_censored_interval` is accepted with a 50-digit reference for its gradient (P6, #78).

entries.what: The value of log Q(shape, x) is right, and so is `gamma_lcdf`'s shape derivative (to 1e-10), but `gamma_lccdf`'s shape derivative is not: brms's right-censored Gamma rows (`gamma_lccdf`, rate = shape / mu) have inexact gradients in log(shape). brms's interval rows use `gamma_lcdf` and are accurate here.
entries.observed: Gradient in (log mu, log shape) of one right-censored row: y = 7, mu = 5, shape = 5: (3.691412255656, -0.4868664317708), 1.2e-2 relative off in log(shape); y = 2, mu = 5, shape = 10: 2.5e-4; y = 3, mu = 2, shape = 2: 6.1e-5. On the frozen case `gamma_censored_interval`: up to 2.8e-5.
entries.expected: (3.691412255645, -0.4809855583225), 0.02945472493298 and -0.2673022227384 in log(shape), from fourth-order differences of R's `pgamma(., lower.tail = FALSE, log.p = TRUE)` (accurate to about 1e-11); the left-censored and interval rows agree to 1e-10.
entries.fix: Compute the shape derivative of log Q(a, x) to double precision, e.g. from the derivative of log P (series for x < a + 1, `dQ/da = -dP/da`) and the continued fraction of Q differentiated through its recurrence above, iterated to machine precision; or by quadrature of `int_x^inf log(t) t^(a - 1) exp(-t) dt`.

entries.title: Stan's `von_mises_lpdf` overflows (`cyl_bessel_i` numeric overflow) for kappa above about 713.9
entries.what: The density's normalising constant I0(kappa) is evaluated itself and overflows, so `log_prob` raises an error (and a fit cannot start) for a precision above about 713.9, where the density is ordinary. brms's R-side `dvon_mises` (log_lik) is exact there.
entries.observed: One row y = 0.1 at mu = 0: kappa = 700 and 713 within 8.4e-14 of the exact value; kappa = 714, 720, 1000: "Exception: Error in function boost::math::cyl_bessel_i<double>(double,double): numeric overflow".
entries.fix: Never form I0(kappa): `log I0(kappa) = kappa + log(i0e(kappa))` with the exponentially scaled Bessel function (or the large-kappa asymptotic series), so the log density is `kappa (cos(y - mu) - 1) - log(2 pi) - log(i0e(kappa))`.

entries.title: loo's `stacking_weights()` stops short of the optimum (weights off by up to 3.7e-4, no exact zeros)

found.note: Stacking is withheld in AutoBayes pending a decision; on the frozen case `gauss_loo_compare_x_stacking` brms's weights are 1.04e-8 from the optimum.

entries.what: The stacking objective is maximised by `stats::constrOptim` (a log-barrier method) and the result returned at its tolerance, so the weights are near, not at, the optimum, and a model the optimum excludes keeps a small positive weight.
entries.observed: Seeded pointwise elpd sets: `two_nearly_equal` loo (0.999630903495, 0.000369096505); `five_200` up to 7e-5 off with 1.5e-7 on an excluded model; `four_one_dominated` 9.4e-6 off with 1.7e-8 on the excluded model; objective up to 2e-6 below the optimum's.
entries.expected: (1, 0) for `two_nearly_equal`, exact zeros for excluded models, and the KKT optimum of `sum_i log(sum_k w_k exp(lpd_ik))` on the simplex (computed in the script by multiplicative updates and active-set Newton steps).
entries.fix: Solve the stacking problem to its KKT conditions (`g_k = sum_i exp(lpd_ik) / p_i` equal to N on the support and at most N off it), e.g. by an active-set Newton method on the simplex, which gives exact zeros.

entries.title: loo's MCSE of an observation's elpd_loo is NaN once that elpd is below about -372
entries.what: The Monte Carlo standard error of elpd_loo_i is NaN once its square on the probability scale underflows, and the total MCSE with it; elpd_loo, p_loo and k-hat are unaffected. Shifting the observation's log-likelihood by a constant shifts elpd_loo_i and leaves every other per-observation quantity unchanged, so its MCSE should not change either.
entries.observed: 1000 draws x 5 observations, the fifth near -400: its `mcse_elpd_loo` is NaN and `print()` says "MCSE of elpd_loo is NaN."
entries.expected: 0.0134962534892, the MCSE of the same column shifted by +400 (whose elpd_loo, -0.0836882186983, is the original's plus 400, and whose p_loo and k-hat are identical).
entries.fix: Evaluate the MCSE after subtracting `max_s log p_is` from the observation's log-likelihood (the MCSE is invariant to that shift), or carry the log-normal approximation's terms relative to `exp(elpd_loo_i)`, so that nothing squares `exp(elpd_loo_i)`.

entries.title: A one-row model with `trunc()` (a per-row or a constant bound) cannot be built: rstan stops at data initialisation

found.note: Found while writing U22, whose truncated rows use two identical rows for this reason.

entries.what: With a single data row, `make_standata()` gives the truncation bound `lb` as a plain number (no dim) while the program declares it with length N = 1, so rstan refuses the data ("mismatch in number dimensions declared and found in context ... variable name=lb; dims declared=(1); dims found=()") and `brm()` returns an object without a valid model. Rare in practice, but it breaks one-row checks and examples.
entries.observed: `y | trunc(lb = L) ~ 1` and `y | trunc(lb = 1) ~ 1` with one row (y = 1.5, L = 1): the rstan error above at `brm(..., chains = 0)`, then "the model object is not created or not valid" from `log_prob`.
entries.expected: A model whose log likelihood at mu = 0, sigma = 1 is `log phi(1.5) - log(1 - Phi(1))` = -0.2029168881954091, as the same model with two identical rows gives twice that (brms -0.4058337763908186) and a one-row model without truncation gives `log phi(1.5)` (brms -2.043938533204672, exact).
entries.fix: Pass the bounds (and any other per-row data entry) to Stan as arrays of length N even when N = 1, e.g. with `as.array()`, as brms already does for the response.
